what: Seven openwork balustrade or stair-rail posts, called 石柱 or 'columns' in the press; white marble with relief flowers and scrolling geometric ornament, about 0.8 to 0.92 m high
from_where_stated: Xiyang Lou by comparison with ornament still on site; the park's 刘阳 lists 养雀笼, 谐奇趣, 海晏堂, 方外观 (snippet only); no single building is proved
now_at: Yuanmingyuan: shown at 正觉寺 from 13 Oct 2023; 圆明园博物馆
now_place_zh: 圆明园遗址公园 正觉寺 最上楼 一层 (2023 exhibition)
moved: Left China in the Republic according to the 2023 authentication; Munthe (1864-1935) shipped objects to Bergen from 1907; part held back in the USA after an attempted sale to the Los Angeles County museum in 1926; given to the Bergen museum 1961-64; arrived Beijing 20 June 2023, handed to the park 21 June 2023
status_today: In the park's collection. 2.6 tonnes together.
note: CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: the 2014 reports said they would go to Peking University in autumn 2014. That did not happen: the agreement dates from December 2013, and the columns reached Beijing only in June 2023, and went to the park, not to PKU, which co-hosted the show. Also: the common phrase 'looted 1860' sits badly with the same report's statement that the holder got them in the Republic; S812: 'It is not known how Munthe acquired the columns'. Removal from a ruin after 1860 is likelier than loot in 1860: inference, C. Seven of 21 at KODE, so 14 stayed in Bergen (S812).

what: V&A C.382-1912: glazed shell with scrolls and leaf at the sides, on a triangular plan, 34.5 × 38 × 23 cm. The record's material says stoneware with turquoise glaze, its description earthenware: conflict inside the record

now_place_zh: 伦敦 维多利亚与艾伯特博物馆

note: Best-dated physical witness of glazed ornament found: viewed (research look). Shows the form and the colour. Not looted in 1860: gathered in 1912, so the press's sweep over 'looted' does not apply. Wylde's attribution to Kangxi and to French Jesuits is wrong on the date.
